home.aboutHeading: Lexnova — Law That Shapes the Future
home.aboutBody: Lexnova is a legal innovation research center where academic knowledge, practical experience, and modern technology meet. Our mission is to advance practice-oriented legal education — from AI and cyberlaw to compliance and sustainable development.
home.noNews: No news has been published yet.

about.headline: A legal education center, in public.
about.intro1: Legal Innovation Research Center — Lexnova is a modern space for professional education, research, and practical development. Our goal is to present law not only as a system of norms, but as a tool for protecting rights and creating innovative solutions. Lexnova combines academic depth, practical experience, and a future-oriented vision.
about.intro2: The Center's work spans law's fundamental, contemporary, and interdisciplinary fields, including administrative, tax, civil, criminal, labor, corporate, transport, energy, artificial intelligence, and technology law. Lexnova's distinctive areas include the anthropology, philosophy, and sociology of law, legal culture, education law, children's rights, sustainable development law, media law, and medical law, as well as cultural heritage protection law. Our teaching is built on academic rigor, practical applicability, and innovative approaches, turning legal knowledge into practical skills and professional opportunity.
about.mission1: Lexnova's mission is to develop modern, practice-oriented, and innovative legal education that combines academic knowledge, professional experience, research, and technological progress. We create a professional and intellectual space where lawyers, students, researchers, and representatives of the public and private sectors gain current knowledge, develop practical skills, and prepare for today's legal challenges.
about.mission2: Lexnova places particular importance on the intersection of law, technology, business, and societal development — including artificial intelligence, cyber law, personal data protection, compliance, and sustainable development. Our mission is to turn knowledge into real professional opportunity and to develop specialists who can meet today's legal challenges with knowledge, practical skill, and innovative thinking.
about.vision1: Lexnova's vision is to become a leading, trusted, and innovative center for legal education and research — one that fosters the creation of new knowledge, the development of law, and the establishment of high professional standards. We are building a space where academic knowledge, practical experience, technological progress, and interdisciplinary approaches come together, giving professionals and future lawyers the ability to understand and effectively respond to today's challenges.
about.vision2: Our vision is to cultivate an environment that fosters critical and innovative thinking, professional responsibility, and the exchange of knowledge — bringing together students, researchers, and practitioners, and strengthening collaboration with local and international professional networks. For Lexnova, the law of the future is one grounded in knowledge, innovation, the protection of human rights, and responsible governance — a law that responds to social and technological change and lays the foundation for sustainable development.
about.objective1: Expanding access to modern, high-quality, practice-oriented legal education and professional development.
about.objective2: Delivering trainings, certificate programs, public lectures, and interdisciplinary educational projects that respond to today's professional needs.
about.objective3: Advancing research and teaching in both classical and contemporary fields of law, including technology, artificial intelligence, cyber law, personal data protection, compliance, ESG, and sustainable development.
about.objective4: Building critical and analytical thinking, practical skills, professional ethics, and a culture of legal research — particularly by supporting young lawyers and researchers.
about.objective5: Promoting local and international collaboration and knowledge-sharing, and contributing to raising the quality of legal education, research, and professional development in Georgia.

faq.q1: How do I register for a course or training?
faq.a1: Open the program page and use Register while registration is open. If you are not signed in, you will be asked to log in (or create a student account) and then returned to the program to complete enrollment.
faq.a2: Participants who complete a course or training receive a LexNova certificate of completion by email. Workshops that have already closed can request a reissue from {email}.
faq.a3: Fees are listed on each program page. We will send payment instructions after you register. Group bookings for a workplace cohort can be invoiced; write to us with the program name and headcount.
faq.q4: Is attendance required? Can I join online?
faq.a4: Check the format on the program page. Hybrid sessions can be joined in the Civic Classroom or live online. Online-only programs have no in-person seat. We expect attendance at the sessions you book.
faq.a5: Cancellations more than fourteen days before the start date are refunded in full. After that, we can transfer your place to a later edition of the same program where one exists. Write to {email} with your name and the program title.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This placeholder policy explains, in plain language, how LexNova expects to handle personal information on this site: names, email addresses, account details, and course registrations. It is a draft for development, not a finished legal document.

whoWeAre.heading: Who we are
whoWeAre.p1: {name} is a legal-education site. For this draft, the contact point for privacy questions is {email}. The postal address on the site is {address}. Replace these details with the real controller name, registration, and address before launch.

whatWeCollect.heading: What we collect
whatWeCollect.p1: When you create an account we store your full name, email address, and a hashed password held by our authentication provider. We also store the role of your account (student, teacher, or admin).
whatWeCollect.p2: When you register for a course or training we store which program you joined, when you registered, and whether that registration is confirmed or cancelled.
whatWeCollect.p3: When you send the contact form we store your name, email address, and message so we can reply.
whatWeCollect.p4: We do not ask for payment card numbers on this site in the current build. If payments are added later, this policy must be updated.

whyWeUse.heading: Why we use it
whyWeUse.p1: We use this information to create and secure your account, to enroll you in programs, to show you your courses and calendar, to answer messages, and to let administrators manage the catalog and registrations.
whyWeUse.p2: We rely on steps you take (creating an account, submitting a form, or registering for a program) and on our interest in running the school. A lawyer should name the correct legal bases for the jurisdiction where LexNova launches.

whoSees.heading: Who else sees it
whoSees.p1: Site administrators can see profiles and registration history in order to run programs. Lecturers listed on public pages are a separate directory; linking a lecturer record to a login is optional.
whoSees.p2: The site is hosted with a cloud provider and uses a database and authentication service. Those processors see the data needed to keep the site running. Name the actual processors in this section before launch.
whoSees.p3: We do not sell your name or email. We do not currently share registrations with advertisers.

howLong.heading: How long we keep it
howLong.p1: Account and registration records stay for as long as the account exists and for a period afterwards that a lawyer should set (for example, to show who attended a course). Contact messages are kept so we can follow up, then deleted or archived on a schedule you choose before launch.

choices.heading: Your choices
choices.p1: You can update your name and password from your dashboard profile. To correct other details, close an account, or ask what we hold, email us. Depending on where you live you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict processing, and to complain to a supervisory authority. Those rights need jurisdiction-specific wording before launch.

children.heading: Children
children.p1: This site is aimed at adults taking professional or civic education. It is not intended for children. If you believe we have collected information from a child, contact us so we can delete it.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.p1: When this draft is replaced by a reviewed policy, we will update the date on this page. Material changes should be announced in a way a lawyer recommends.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These placeholder terms describe how you may use the LexNova website, create an account, and register for courses or trainings. They are a draft for development, not a contract you can rely on, and they are not legal advice.

theSite.heading: The site
theSite.p1: {name} publishes information about legal-education programs and lets signed-in users register for those programs. Teaching materials, schedules, and fees shown on the site may change. Nothing on the site is legal advice for your own matter.

accounts.heading: Accounts
accounts.p1: You must provide a real name and a working email address when you register. You are responsible for keeping your password confidential and for activity on your account. We may suspend an account that is used to harm the site, other students, or the integrity of a program.

registrations.heading: Course registrations
registrations.p1: Submitting a registration request records your name and email against that program. Registration may close when a course is full, when a deadline passes, or when an administrator cancels a place. Completing a registration on this site does not, by itself, create a right to a certificate, a refund, or a particular timetable — those rules belong in a reviewed student agreement before launch.

acceptableUse.heading: Acceptable use
acceptableUse.p1: Do not misuse the site: no scraping that overloads our systems, no attempts to access other people's accounts or admin tools, and no posting of content you do not have the right to share. Program descriptions and news articles on the site remain our (or our licensors') materials.

disclaimers.heading: Disclaimers
disclaimers.p1: The site is provided as a working draft. We do not warrant that it is uninterrupted or error-free. To the extent a lawyer later permits, liability for use of this development site should be limited. Do not use these placeholder terms as a cap on liability in production.

governingLaw.heading: Governing law
governingLaw.p1: Name the country or state whose law applies, and the courts that would hear a dispute, before launch. This draft does not choose a jurisdiction.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.p1: Questions about these terms can be sent to {email}.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: This placeholder policy describes the cookies this site sets today. LexNova does not currently run advertising or analytics cookies. A lawyer should confirm whether this notice is enough for the place you launch.

whatWeUse.heading: What cookies we use
whatWeUse.p1: Essential cookies keep you signed in. They are set by our authentication provider when you log in, register, or reset a password, and they are needed for the dashboard, course registration, and admin tools to work.
whatWeUse.p2: If you dismiss the cookie notice on this site, we store a first-party preference cookie (lexnova_cookie_notice) so we do not show that banner again on this browser. That cookie is not used for advertising.
whatWeUse.p3: We do not currently set cookies for advertising, social-media pixels, or third-party analytics. If those are added later, this policy and the banner must be updated — and consent may be required before they run.

howLong.heading: How long they last
howLong.p1: Sign-in cookies last for the session length our authentication provider uses, including “remember this browser” behaviour if you stay logged in. The cookie-notice preference cookie is stored for up to one year.

control.heading: How to control cookies
control.p1: You can delete cookies in your browser settings. Clearing essential cookies will sign you out. Blocking all cookies may stop login and registration from working.
control.p2: You can read this policy again from the footer at any time. The privacy policy explains the personal data we store in our database, which is separate from these cookies.
